checks.finding: All fourteen in-scope requirements (REQ-001–REQ-014) are observable or measurable. Each maps to at least one AC whose assertion names a concrete oracle: schema acceptance of a specific tuple, fixture rejection with named conditions, evidence record field enumeration, digest equality, cardinality counts, named status values. REQ-004 unambiguously defines the characteristic-override namespace ('credential_bearing' and 'release_write') and schema boundary (additive optional list on component and shared-path records with four exact fields). All OQs are resolved and their resolutions are normative. No requirement depends on an unresolved design decision that would block verification.

Every stated goal has at least one matching acceptance criterion. REQ-001: AC-001, AC-002. REQ-002: AC-003, AC-004. REQ-003: AC-005, AC-006, AC-032. REQ-004: AC-007, AC-030, AC-031. REQ-005: AC-008, AC-009. REQ-006: AC-010, AC-011, AC-027. REQ-007: AC-012, AC-013. REQ-008: AC-014, AC-015, AC-028, AC-033. REQ-009: AC-016, AC-017, AC-018, AC-034. REQ-010: AC-019, AC-029. REQ-011: AC-020, AC-021. REQ-012: AC-022, AC-023, AC-024. REQ-013: AC-025. REQ-014: AC-026. All 34 acceptance criteria maintain full forward and reverse traceability to requirements and tests.

All 34 acceptance criteria describe externally observable behavior, state, or artifact changes. AC-030 specifies exact counts, scopes, machine names, and values for the live overrides. AC-031 defines three distinct negative fixtures (unknown name, out-of-scope, no-op) with concrete rejection conditions. AC-001 to AC-029 and AC-032 to AC-034 provide explicit oracles including schema acceptance, digest matching, field enumeration, and cardinality-triggered branch re-evaluation. None rely on invisible internal process state.

The Non-goals section explicitly excludes: (1) creating live sdd/ files during specification bootstrap; (2) implementing later desktop, cloud-service, or durable-workflow Packs; (3) replacing existing Registry/ownership resolver/Facet Manifest/approval machinery; (4) adding UI, cloud deployment, or new CI workflows; (5) approving this spec, tasks, approval sidecars, or WFIs. REQ-004 explicitly bounds the characteristic override namespace and schema extension to two record types and two machine names.

Material constraints are explicitly stated across security, data, compatibility, migration, and promotion dimensions: HMAC-bound approval sidecar required (REQ-001); atomic two-axis Phase-2 transition (REQ-008); registry-cardinality-dependent rollback branching (REQ-009); nine-component closed set (OQ-001); closed path ownership (OQ-002); additive characteristic override namespace and four-field schema constraint (REQ-004); A1-A8 merge/usability prerequisite before live changes (REQ-011, REQ-014); and four mechanically checkable promotion preconditions (OQ-003).

Each high-risk claim carries a planned validation surface: approval-sidecar bypass (AC-002, AC-016-018); premature required enforcement (AC-012, AC-013, AC-033 with three negative fixtures); Pack duplication (AC-008, AC-009, OQ-006 reference composition); rollback governance unusability (AC-016, AC-017, AC-034); over-broad ownership hiding boundaries (AC-005, AC-006, AC-032); and override mechanism drift (AC-030, AC-031).
